Can you look into an arithmetic explanation for G3

I’ll look for an arithmetic reason for G3’s small residual defect, starting from the signed source and correction formulas. I’ll distinguish any new cancellation estimate from the existing source-informed numerical bound.

There is a concrete arithmetic candidate: the finite sum omits the first Stirling correction and the next Gaussian heat-curvature term. Those give an explicit correction to every retained mode, with no fitted coefficients. I’m checking how much of the residual they explain and what remains in the Riemann–Siegel edge term.

At the pilot center, the finite gamma/heat correction has defect about \(+1.3344\times10^{-4}\), while the Riemann–Siegel edge contributes about \(-1.3603\times10^{-4}\). Their difference gives the observed \(-2.5881\times10^{-6}\).

That particularly strong cancellation is local; it varies across the box. The finite-mode correction now has an independent uniform remainder bound. The complete edge remainder is still needed for a uniform G3 estimate.
